fixed.problem: W15-24: a CLI tool was sent back three times for the usage exit its own criterion asks for. The sentence 'node wc.js on a file containing ...' ran a bare `node wc.js`, and expectsError read only that one sentence.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/verification.test.ts 'w15-review, wave 15' > 'W15-24: live check 2's word counter is Done after one run ...' (before: revise then escalate x3); packages/runtime/test/try-plan.test.ts 'w15-review, wave 15' (three W15-24 cases)
fixed.how: try-plan.ts now has two word lists. GOES_ON words (verbs and the like) end a command, as before. A CONNECTORS word (on, in, for, with, from, at, by, to, against, using, ...) after a command with no written argument marks it `described`. commandsIn leaves described commands out. A script that listens is still started. 'with no ...' and 'without ...' count as a bare run. A bare run (no args, no stdin) gets expectsError when any sentence of the brief, the criteria or the README says a run with no argument fails (NO_ARGUMENT plus EXPECTS_ERROR). The measured-problem rule (ADR 0104) is unchanged. ADR 0110 amended.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Bench: create a coder task 'Build wc.js command line word counter' with live check 2's outcome and six criteria (criterion 1: "node wc.js on a file containing 'hello world foo' prints 3"; criterion 4: 'Running with no argument prints a usage message to stderr and exits with code 1'), then Start. Expect Done · Reviewed and tried after one run. 'See what was checked' should list only 'node wc.js <file>: worked', with no bare 'node wc.js: had a problem'. Live check 3 (step S6): brief 'A command line tool that counts the words in a file. Usage: node wc.js <file>.', Approve and start. Expect Done · Reviewed and tried after one run, no 'Sent back: Tried node wc.js' line in the session log, and the dependent test task runs.

For a web-reading specialist, retryConstraints drops any open finding that names a host the rule refuses (webRuleRefuses, hostsNamedIn) and adds WEB_RULE_WINS_LINE. ADR 0107 amended.

fixed.problem: W15-27 (TR-15): a review refused at the project's budget paused the task with 'The work is done; its review waits for room in the budget.', but after the budget was raised the specialist ran again before the review.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/budget-pause.test.ts 'w15-review, wave 15' > 'W15-27: after the budget is raised, the paused review is done without running the coder again' and '... the same across a restart between the pause and the raise' (both failed with the old runner). New: '... work that changed while the review waited is done again', and packages/capabilities/test/pr-executor.test.ts 'w15-review, wave 15' prepareReview.
fixed.how: Built as ADR 0112's TR-15 design. session/review-pending.ts keeps a `reviewPending` entry on the work run's Run row: attempt, specialist, summary, report, changedFiles, PR, branch, webRule, searchSeen, and workHash (a sha256 over the changed files as they are in the workspace). The runner writes it at a budget refusal and also at a credential refusal (same class), via keepForReview. Before execute, reviewOnlyResult takes the latest work run's entry if the attempt is unchanged, executor.prepareReview(task) makes the workspace ready, and workHash matches. The entry is cleared either way. The kept result (reviewOnly: true) goes straight to review: no task.started, task.files, task.finished or onTaskFinished, and heard lines and queue notes are not used up. prepareReview: PrTaskExecutor (one appended method) puts a repo task's worktree back on its branch and returns a project folder as is. LoopTaskExecutor returns its worktree. In a project folder whose session-end commit already took the work, GitDiffPort.diffFor(..., {taskFiles}) diffs the task's files since its last 'Workspace before' snapshot. Anything else falls back to today's rerun. ADR 0112 amended; user guide updated.

notes_for_other_areas: W15-27 LANDED (for w15-words, W15-65): 'review_waits' now means the next session reviews the kept result without running the specialist again, as long as the attempt and the changed files are unchanged. So the card's 'The work is done; its review waits for room in the budget.' (request-words.ts pausedWorkSentence) is true now and needs no rewording for truth. When the files changed, the specialist runs again first. A review refused by a credential is kept the same way.

runner.ts (w15-run owns recordStep and addCost): this area wrapped executor.execute as `result = kept ?? (await this.deps.executor.execute({...}))`, where `kept` comes from reviewOnlyResult(task) right after the in_progress transition. sayStarted, task.files, task.finished and onTaskFinished are skipped when result.reviewOnly. heard and notes are not consumed by the pass. The critic.verdict emit gains a `blocking` field. TaskExecutionResult gains `webRule?` and `reviewOnly?`. The TaskExecutor interface gains `prepareReview?(task)`. Keep all of these at merge.

executor.ts (w15-run owns searchPlanFor, the pause rule and cost): this area added `todayLine` to the brief constraints, `webRule` to the returned results (the paused one too, which now also returns webSources and searchSeen), reviewSourcesArtifact beside webSourceArtifact in both drivers' Run artifacts, the retryConstraints `refusesHost` option (webRuleRefuses, hostsNamedIn, WEB_RULE_WINS_LINE) and LoopTaskExecutor.prepareReview.
pr-executor.ts: only one appended method, PrTaskExecutor.prepareReview(task), at the end of the class (it checks out the task's branch in its worktree if needed; no commit, no push).

Run row artifacts gain two entries: `reviewSources` (page text kept for later reviews; never served to a screen; runWebSources reads only `webSources`) and `reviewPending` (the kept result for the review-only pass).

Model-facing texts added (code, test the exact text): critic section 'Web pages research may read (the project's rule the worker ran under)' plus WEB_RULE_TRUST_LINE; critic.md 1.3.0 bullet; WEB_RULE_WINS_LINE in retry briefs; "Today's date is YYYY-MM-DD (<tz>)." in every brief; ', read <date> <time> UTC' on web_fetch results; 'Today: <date> (UTC)' in the intake request; review-only artifact 'this review is of the run above, which finished in an earlier session; its review waited for room in the budget, and the work has not changed since'; new onlyWebsitesLines and NO_WEB_RULE texts; specialist prompts 1.1.0 ('Write the file the brief names (`answer.md` when it names none)').

Person-facing sentences changed (old -> new): (1) event-lines critic.verdict sent back: 'The critic sent "X" back: <summary's first 100 chars>. Trying again.' -> 'The critic sent "X" back: <the review's blocking finding>. Trying again.' (2) try-page: 'the browser did not start (<Playwright text>)' -> 'the browser did not start within a minute; the page was judged from its files', or 'the browser did not start; the page was judged from its files'. (3) project-checks: '... that no check ran: its package.json names no test script' -> '... : there is no package.json to run them' when there is none, '... : its package.json cannot be read' when it cannot be parsed, unchanged otherwise. (4) critic ruled summary for a rule's 'human': model words -> 'Waits for you: the report asks you something. <model words>' or 'Waits for your sign-off. <model words>'. (5) Tasks tab Critic column: 'accepted' beside failed or marked-done tasks -> 'Not reviewed' / 'Failed review' / '—'. (6) Drawer: markdown table rows -> 'cell · cell · cell'. (7) user-guide paragraphs on paused reviews and research dates.

For w15-words: a review-only pass's session log has only the critic's verdict line. If you want a line saying the waiting review went on (e.g. 'The review of "X" goes on: its work was done in an earlier session.'), add a payload or event in the event-lines area you own; runner.ts does not emit one today.
